## TASK-003 - Author a neutral versioned Curator integration recipe

Add reviewed declarative recipe, locator map and competency specification to ONTOLOGY-depo/integrations/curator/1.0.0 and reference it from CURATION-depo contract resources. The recipe emits only destination-local records with the selected namespace; keep neutral canonical starter graphs empty and sys4ai-core 1.0.0 locked. Implement a pure deterministic renderer in the ontology owner for use by both initializer and root integration preview; it returns bytes and diagnostics without writing, invoking destination code or granting authority. Derive installed-source hashes only after destination specialization settles.

### Risks

- Recipe is declarative reference data, not an additional ontology module import; source binding locators must resolve after destination packages are final.

### Acceptance criteria

- Recipe has stable local suffixes for process, function capabilities, sources, role definitions, scopes and prerequisite artifacts; explicit local typed predicates cover consumes, produces, maintains, coordinatesOwner and triggeredBy where core predicates do not fit.
- Each function has direct current-source bindings and an observable competency query; graph references resolve after deterministic destination specialization.
- Neutral inputs contain no root identity, native actor, Task instance, backlog, learned data, runtime result or bound publication authority.
- Pure render rejects missing/changed sources, unresolved locators, malformed recipes, namespace/ID collisions, invalid role pairs and duplicate records before any target write. Identical recipe, identity and final source bytes produce identical output.

### Planned verification

- Validate recipe/manifest closure and duplicate IDs; render two different project namespaces and compare only expected specialization differences.
- Validate the rendered graph with unchanged core profile domain/range, source locator, ambiguity and namespace checks; reject unsupported recipes/imports.

## TASK-004 - Implement exact ontology-owned integration and recovery

Implement the reviewed integrate-curator version-1 operation within the existing ontology owner. Provide integration_preview(root, selection), integration_publish(root, proposal, grant, expected_preview_sha256) and integration_recover(root, operation_id, grant), with explicit CLI routes and guarded adapters under the existing ontology family. Limit changes to the three reserved integration files and exact additive ontology.yaml project_files/binding_files/competency_files/source_allowlist entries. Validate the complete candidate config and graph in memory through a narrow internal loader path. Keep ordinary load_project overrides, legacy publication/grants, identity, context, imports, retrieval settings, profiles and bound publication scope unchanged.

### Risks

- Existing publication cannot select new config paths, so the new bounded adoption interface must be implemented and reviewed; do not pretend it already exists.
- Static fixture actors never authorize live root or destination writes.

### Acceptance criteria

- Proposal binds exact integration recipe/renderer/helper hashes, config predecessor, authored inventory, source locators, graph pre/post bytes and current native owner scope. Config selection is a separately named integration-adoption operation; ordinary publish retains its configured-file-only contract.
- New selected paths are ONTOLOGY/modules/project/curator.jsonld, ONTOLOGY/bindings/curator.jsonld and ONTOLOGY/modules/project/curator-competency.json; collisions fail unless exact receipt-owned compatible records are selected for refresh.
- The existing ontology intent/receipt/recovery area retains all original preimages and completion states. No second Task/setup ledger or replacement graph is introduced.
- Disabled publication, incompatible current authority, enabled-guard stale context or missing prerequisite returns an exact hold; none is enabled or bypassed. Initial empty installation uses the setup owner's explicit reviewed starter scope; existing authored ontology is changed only by its current ontology owner.
- The new exact integration grant uses its own named contract and validates a current Director or confirmed manager, real native observation/expiry, governing hashes, exact operation and proposal/preview/config hashes, exact selected config/record changes and manager overlap. It is never converted to or authorized by an existing publish grant that lacks config scope.
- Existing publication disabled settings remain disabled and block required authored-ontology writes. An initial absent/pristine starter install uses only its reviewed setup authority; it does not mint a persistent ontology grant or claim live publication.
- Partial recovery recognizes only original config/graph pre/post bytes, the same recipe/selection and current owner grant. Readers diagnose an incomplete selection accurately. Setup waits for the linked ontology completion receipt and semantic readiness before success; stale bindings and unrelated source changes cannot be hidden by config replacement.

### Planned verification

- Test unchanged core publication compatibility and new owner positive path with actual isolated native-owner-shaped fixture evidence clearly classified as fixtures.
- Reject config changes to project identity, imports, retrieval limits, profiles, grants, source allowlists outside exact recipe needs and graph paths outside selected scope.
- Fault after each config/graph/receipt replacement; recover identical pre/post states once and reject changed source, target, owner generation or payload.
- Verify new integration-preview is read-only and validates proposed config together with the graph before any write; ordinary preview still rejects ontology.yaml and unselected paths.
- Exercise both initialized Director and confirmed-manager cases, config-scope refusal, disabled publication, conflicting live writer, stale native/grant/helper context and unchanged guard semantics. Keep native-shaped fixture identities explicitly classified as fixtures.

Bind current operational sources, not current Task actors, and retain all bounded read diagnostics.

### Risks

- Existing availability means source freshness; a current record alone must not appear runtime-operational.

### Acceptance criteria

- capability curator and per-function queries return function purpose, inputs, outputs, responsible owner route, scope and prerequisites with exact source/hash/version context.
- Relationship/current queries answer maintenance targets, evaluation triggers and governing rules. Task current ownership remains a required live owner check, never an asserted stored actor.
- Missing, stale, ambiguous and unsupported functions remain explicit; read operations leave canonical/config/runtime/generated files and persistent timestamps unchanged.

### Planned verification

- Run positive competency queries and stale source, unavailable locator, ambiguous alias, unsupported-operation and result-bound controls.
- Hash and timestamp all selected files before/after capability, knowledge --intent current and neighbors/path reads; exercise current-source excerpt drift.
